concepts.def: First five books of Jewish scripture (the Tanakh).
Jewish place of worship and learning.
Jewish day of rest, Friday sunset–Saturday sunset.
Cabinet in synagogue holding the Torah scrolls.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Torah is the first five books of the Tanakh: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy. It contains stories, laws and teachings. In synagogues it is read from a handwritten scroll kept in a cabinet called the Ark.

The synagogue is a place of prayer, study and community. Jews come together to read the Torah, pray and learn. The service is led by a rabbi or other prayer leader. Men often wear a kippah (skullcap) and a tallit (prayer shawl).

Shabbat is the Jewish day of rest, from Friday sunset to Saturday sunset. Families light candles, share a special meal with bread (challah) and wine, attend synagogue and avoid work. It celebrates God resting after creating the world.
